title: Soft-Body Tug-of-War Arena
description: A robot and soldier stand on opposite ends of a deformable soft-body terrain bridge made of interconnected spring-mass nodes. The user manipulates gravity zones, applies directional force impulses, and toggles anchor points to shift the soft-body mass distribution, trying to tilt the bridge so one character slides toward the other. An energy conservation meter tracks total kinetic and potential energy, and full undo/redo of every interaction step is supported.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a soft-body tug-of-war simulation. Load robot.glb and soldier.glb using GLTFLoader, placing the robot at x=-6 and the soldier at x=+6, both standing on a soft-body bridge. The bridge is a 20x5 grid of particle nodes connected by damped springs rendered as a deformable mesh (BufferGeometry updated each frame). Each node has mass, position, velocity, and is subject to gravity and spring forces. Total system energy (kinetic + potential + elastic) is computed and displayed in a HUD conservation meter; deviations above 2% trigger a warning. Camera: PerspectiveCamera at (0,8,14) looking at origin, with OrbitControls. Lighting: one DirectionalLight with shadows, one HemisphereLight. Interactions (10-14 steps expected): 1) Click a node to toggle it as a fixed anchor (up to 4 anchors). 2) Right-click drag on the bridge to apply a directional force impulse to nearby nodes. 3) Press G then click a region to place a local gravity attractor or repulsor (toggle with Shift). 4) Press T to adjust global gravity strength via a slider overlay. 5) Press C to couple the robot or soldier model to the nearest bridge node so they ride the deformation. 6) Full undo/redo stack (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) recording every anchor toggle, force impulse, gravity zone placement, coupling change, and gravity adjustment. Each undo restores full particle state. Display step counter, energy bar, and undo/redo depth. Characters should gently bob with the mesh deformation beneath them using vertical offset interpolation. Spring damping coefficient adjustable via UI slider. Use requestAnimationFrame with fixed-timestep Verlet integration at 60 substeps per frame for stability.
